what.text: Using biotin for hair loss is off-label, and there is little research on it.

research.text: There is little good research on biotin for hair loss. A 2024 review found only three studies of oral biotin for hair, and said its use is not supported by high-quality studies.

research.title: Oral biotin for hair growth or quality

facts.v: Literature review; case reports and case series left out

research.found: The best study, double-blind and placebo-controlled, found no difference between biotin and placebo for hair growth. The other two, in people on isotretinoin and in women after weight-loss surgery, were open to bias and did not show clear benefit.

src.label: Yelich et al., J Clin Aesthet Dermatol, 2024 (review)

research.title: Oral biotin, topical minoxidil, or both, on hair growth speed

facts.v: Randomized, open-label, self-controlled crossover; each man had all three treatments in turn
Hair growth speed and scalp area covered, from photos of a shaved patch

research.found: Biotin alone and minoxidil alone did not change growth speed. Only the two together showed a faster rate over 14 days. The men did not have hair loss, and the authors list the small sample as a limit.

src.label: Valentim et al., An Bras Dermatol, 2024

us.text: In the US, biotin is sold as a dietary supplement, not as an approved drug for hair loss.
FDA does not approve dietary supplements before they are sold. Vitamins count as dietary ingredients.

src.label: Questions and answers on dietary supplements, FDA

us.text: In FDA’s drug approval records, biotin appears as one of many vitamins in approved intravenous multivitamin products, such as M.V.I. Adult. We found no FDA-approved biotin product for hair loss.

The strips Adonis carries through Beluga are a compounded prescription product, not a supplement. Compounded drugs are not FDA approved, and this mix has not been reviewed by FDA for safety or effect.

side.text: Biotin has no FDA drug label. FDA’s main warning is that biotin can make some lab tests wrong.

items.text: Biotin can interfere with certain lab tests and cause wrong results that may not be noticed.

src.label: Biotin interference with troponin lab tests, FDA

items.text: FDA keeps getting reports of falsely low troponin results caused by biotin. Troponin is a blood test used to check for heart attack. FDA lists troponin tests that have not fixed the problem.

src.label: Biotin interference with troponin lab tests, FDA

side.text: The side effects of the other ingredients in the strips (minoxidil and finasteride) are covered on their own pages.

unconfirmed: We could not open FDA’s updated safety communication “The FDA Warns that Biotin May Interfere with Lab Tests” (it has moved to FDA’s archive and did not load); the page cites FDA’s live troponin page instead.
We did not confirm biotin’s status in Canada, the UK, the EU or Australia from a regulator record.
We did not review animal or lab studies of biotin and hair.
surprises: Biotin is widely sold for hair, but the only placebo-controlled study found by a 2024 review showed no difference from placebo.
FDA’s main public warning about biotin is not about hair at all: it can cause falsely low troponin results, a test used to check for heart attack.
